result.overview: Materials cover Nash and strict Nash equilibria, best responses, location games, sequential and repeated games, and payoff transformations. Problem Set 3 supplies questions without solutions; some requested outcomes are therefore not established by the materials.

topics.title: Nash and strict Nash equilibria
topics.summary: Study best-response tests, how multiple equilibria can arise, and why strict equilibria are limited by the number of strategies of the smaller player. Pset 2 gives an example with at most four strict equilibria in a 4×4 game; Pset 3 asks for a maximum in an 8×10 game.

topics.title: Traveler’s Dilemma and preferences
topics.summary: Compare equilibrium reasoning under selfish and utilitarian objectives. Pset 2 analyzes an even-bid variant with a $2 adjustment: equal bids are Nash equilibria and (2,2) is the unique strict one; Pset 3 poses utilitarian variants of the standard game without supplying solutions.

topics.title: Location and coordination games
topics.summary: Study nearest-vendor location choices, including ties, continuous populations, and discrete or nonstandard city shapes. Pset 2 rules out the three-vendor endpoint–midpoint–endpoint profile on a uniform interval and reports no equilibrium for a chopped isosceles triangle; Pset 3 asks about other configurations.

topics.title: Sequential and repeated games
topics.summary: Review backward induction in Hawk–Dove, subgame-perfect incentives in a two-period Prisoner’s Dilemma followed by an Assurance Game, and trigger strategies in repeated Prisoner’s Dilemma. For the supplied infinite-horizon payoff matrix, trigger cooperation requires δ ≥ 1/5.

topics.title: Payoff transformations and zero-sum games
topics.summary: Study why positive affine transformations of each player’s own payoffs preserve Nash equilibria, while zero-sum games can have Nash equilibria—including a game where every outcome is one. The solutions’ claims concern transformations applied consistently across that player’s outcomes.

method: Three fresh production indexer instances. Each cold request is followed by exact same-test cached input on that instance. Provider slot is held across each cold+cached pair; acquisition excluded. The same already-extracted original PDF corpus is used. No question preparation, Jev, microphone or paid voice. Empty application cache does not imply cold provider prompt cache.
followup: Generic v5 topic-oriented description prompt; preserve assumptions and domain restrictions, no subject-specific tuning. Original direct three outputs remain unchanged.
comparison: Explicit 32,000-character direct-path override; all original source text, no map stage. Production default unchanged during this experiment. This is an algorithm comparison, not a quote-repair-only timing change.

assessment.limitation: Three samples of one real corpus, not latency percentiles or a guarantee. Source citation coverage is not exhaustive topic coverage; manual guide review is recorded separately.
